key_insight: VeriFine shows that self-improving embodied agents need judges that can evolve as the agent improves. By scaling verification, the framework can uncover new failures and turn them into better training signals.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the bottleneck caused by fixed evaluation judges in self-improving agents. In embodied reasoning, static judges struggle to verify spatial grounding, causal reasoning, and safety-aware decisions, which limits further improvement.
method: Introduces an agent harness framework called VeriFine to scale verification alongside policy improvement.
Uses adaptive verification to keep judges aligned with newly emerging failure patterns from self-improving agents.
Targets embodied reasoning tasks where reliable assessment must account for spatial, causal, and safety constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means better feedback loops for training embodied agents and more useful failure cases for iterative improvement. It can help produce agents that are more reliable in real-world, safety-sensitive environments.

paper_title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
paper_authors: Zewei Zhou, Rachel Luo, Yulong Cao, Chaowei Xiao, Chensheng Peng
